directive.speaker: agent
directive.quote: Restore and verify the existing c9fbccd8 paid-access grant writer in the declared paid-access owner, retaining immutable grant/revoke behavior while supporting revoke-only requests and admitted byte-bounded writes; use only synthetic checks and normal commit gates.

preserve: The existing access-grant reader shape and immutable subject/grant-reference identities
Conditional creation, idempotent repeats and refusal to change existing terms
Revocations remain monotonic tombstones, including when they arrive before a grant
Output reports accepted writes, not a promise that access is currently held
No payment, buyer, session, credential or network mutation
allowed_deltas: Accept a revoke-only request without requiring an unrelated grant; descriptor and function express the same nonempty either-or rule
Reuse the shared byte-and-row write batcher and refuse a record too large for one admitted message
Add synthetic packed-row and reader consumer checks for revoke-only, tombstones, paired writes, expiry and large Unicode inputs
banned_substitutions: A second grant store or access projection

baseline.scope: Not a source-first port. The writer was authored with its descriptor and tests in Workshop commit c9fbccd8f03da99611a2a9fa405f7649b310ec85; that commit is authorship history, not a source-only copy baseline or a candidate ancestor.

reader_lineage.relationship: The writer emits the license_access/revoke records this earlier reader consumes. This reader is a different mechanism, not a claimed byte-copy source for the writer.

recovery.relationship: This commit restores the same Workshop writer with adaptations. The original authorship commit is not its ancestor. This is recovery history, not an ancestral exact-copy baseline.

lineage_qualification.boundary: NO_PRIOR_OWNER applies only to the original Workshop-authored manual immutable access-grant record adapter, with the current six-repository and native capability searches retained below. It makes no claim that paid access, checkout grant issuance, grant projection or generic persistence lacked an earlier owner. The restored runtime remains in its existing public file.

job: Write immutable access-grant records and revocation tombstones for a person with conditional creation, repeat safety and optional expiry windows
job_scope: Only the Workshop adapter that validates manual grant/revoke input and conditionally creates immutable access-grant records with stable subject/grant identities and permanent revoke tombstones. This does not claim that grant issuance, grant projection, checkout, record persistence, or paid-access management had no older owner.

authorship.scope: Original Workshop write-side adapter for the existing reader shape. The current owner is restored in place with its present API; no new core, older-source byte-copy claim, or retrospective source-first history is introduced.
authorship.repository_role: The current repository and existing target path; this is the original history of that owner.

distinct_from.why: Synthetic contract-rule tests name GrantAccess terms; they neither implement nor issue immutable manual access-grant records.
Viewer capability context scopes offered UI surfaces; it does not write grants.
Publishes a project placement and its capability access DATA; it does not create or revoke member grant records.
Booking grants name a purchased bookable session and booking parties; they are not paid-access refs or the manual access-grant record writer.
Contract fixtures and rules describe commercial terms, not immutable manual grant persistence.
Archived contract-template code carries GrantAccess terms; it is not a manual grant writer.
Builds a legal document from contract-rule DATA and tests its output; it does not execute access grants.
The existing pure grant reader projects license_access effects, windows and revocations into held refs. This writer supplies its established record shape and does not duplicate that projection.
The existing access reader combines payment-derived access and manual grant projections; it is reused to read results rather than replaced.
Synthetic reader, payment and grant-projection tests are consumers, not an earlier manual record writer.
Describes the existing paid-access package and grant record shape; documentation is not an earlier write-side algorithm.
The searched original rows describe existing access readers and paid-file delivery. The restored grant row calls this canonical writer.
Interprets GrantAccess commercial-contract terms, checkout snapshots and usage. It does not conditionally create subject/grant access-grant records or permanent revoke tombstones.
Published tool descriptors describe callers and their jobs; they do not contain the manual grant writer.
Privacy tests use synthetic rule text; they do not implement paid-access grant persistence.
The existing generic records transport and byte/row batcher are reused. They persist caller-supplied record types and do not own manual grant validation, stable grant identities or revoke policy.

Application DATA configures signed-event rules, access screens and payment bindings. It is not an independent immutable manual access-grant record writer; private application paths remain only in the retained raw search.
Consumes access decisions to gate content; it does not issue manual grant records.
Keeps contact-point facts used by account onboarding; it does not manage immutable manual access-grant records.
Reads account, plan and grant effects for a dashboard; it is a consumer.
Reads and displays activation state; it is not the manual grant record writer.

An older grant/revoke issuer exists here: checkout authors capability.access signed events tied to checkout/provider events, then signs and admits them through the signed-event authority. The manual writer neither replaces that issuer nor repeats its payment/account pipeline; it validates manually supplied subject/access refs into the existing access-grant record shape through the generic records door.
Follow-up automation and onboarding tests consume acquisition events; they do not implement this manual record API.
Hosted app routes resolve funnels, commercial offers and access gates. Their access-grant references are routing/consumer behavior rather than immutable manual grant creation.
Generic resource capability edges and authorization DATA describe transfer rights, not paid-access manual member grants.
Private-object delivery checks current entitlement; its grant references are consumer fixtures.
Generic capability obligations, leases and process scripts enforce execution rights, not the access-grant record schema or this manual writer.
Reads existing account-plan/license effects to show a plan; it does not write manual grants.

The older grant projection, its account/session adapters and gate tests read license_access effects and terminal refs. That reader remains the preserved algorithm owner; the new authored adapter is only its record write side.
Synthetic cohort tests treat an access-grant as an observed acquisition fact for identity stitching; they do not create entitlement records.
Revenue integration tests consume grant/payment facts; they do not own manual immutable grants.
Editable GrantAccess terms build contracts and screens; they do not issue these manual records.
Viewer capability context scopes offered UI surfaces; it does not write grants.

The existing signed-event admission/projection pipeline maps capability.access facts into license_access effects. It is an older generic authority, not this records-door adapter; its signature/admission and payment issuance mechanisms are not reimplemented here.
Historical payment execution evidence describes earlier checkout grant effects; it is neither runtime code nor a manual records writer.
A performance test supplies synthetic grant effects to the older product-access gate; it is a consumer test.
Source/consumer conformance tests inspect existing capability and access owners; they do not implement manual grant writes.
Program DATA conformance tests describe acquisition/access wiring, not a reusable manual grant writer.
Context-scoped tool installation and execution grants reference tool definitions; they are a different resource and API from manually issued paid-access refs.

The existing native record journal, models, conditional persistence and OAuth/standing-grant authority remain generic engine owners. This adapter calls generic record operations and introduces no second store or account/payment authority.
